utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. And on behalf of the Trial Chamber I wish to welcome everybody, everyone back. I hope you've had a good rest, although we are all aware that some of you have been working on filing motions just as we have been working on draft -- the drafting of some of the decisions which will be forthcoming very shortly. So Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record all the accused are here. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon and I think that's about it. Prosecution, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Yes. I understand there are some preliminaries you wish to raise, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And everyone, Your Honours. Just for the audiovisual people I've got some static in my headphones, I don't know if anybody else does. But just for a couple of preliminaries, as the Court and everyone is aware, we have agreed with the Defence to request that we have the first week of October off, which is, as you know, according to our established processes of giving a break to reassess and reassemble and as that's proved, I think very helpful in this last year, I know everyone unanimously requests that first week of October, after a good run from today on. So I wanted to mention that to the Trial Chamber to put that request out. Also, as everyone is aware, we are trying to organise a videolink a week from Friday, and if the Defence could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- work with us on that, that's coming to a head and it's a difficult time difference and other logistical issues. Also, and this -- the next witness is here and ready to go. He had asked us initially for private session but in discussing it with him he didn't have the necessary requirements and so I explained that to him and he agreed to testify in public session. However, I would ask and he'd ask, there was a document that he provided a witness and if I could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to suggest that. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to this break, the first week in October that you are requesting, do you anticipate that ultimately this could result in shortening of your case, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's certainly not going to lengthen it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, if there is one week off, automatically it lengthens the Prosecution case by one week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the time that it'll save us and be able to organise ourselves and as you know, especially with the witnesses that we are bringing, it's a really logistical difficulty getting people here and that's actually the more difficult witnesses have all been sort of pushed to the end and so the more time we have to get ready and to work on that, the better we are. And I think we'll very likely save time by having that time, and I think -- well, I think everyone is aware that having that break with the pressure and the stress that everyone is under is absolutely critical. I mean we've all seen it, how we get on a Friday afternoon or evening session after we have been going week after week, and I think that's an invaluable time savings, I think it saves in argument and it saves in frayed tempers and I know we all appreciate that. And we've been all together a year now and I think we've shown the ability to work hard together and argue hard together and I think one of the reasons that we have been able to do that and get as far as we have is because this procedure that the Court set early on so I can argue for days in support of that procedure, and I know the Defence can too, and I think in the end it does save time and resources and emotions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you're requesting from the 1st?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe it's the 1st through the 5th, Monday through Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll think about it and we'll come back to you in due course. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm taking you back in time to when we received a motion for guidelines regarding interviewing witnesses. This motion, you will recall, was filed time back by the Popovic Defence. Our attention has been drawn to the various parts from transcripts, particularly that of the 11th July, when this matter was briefly debated, and going through the transcript, it's our position that the parties declared themselves to be in agreement with the Prosecution motion for a hearing and ruling regarding interviewing witnesses, so according to us, that Prosecution motion, which was filed to my knowledge on the 6th of July, is now moot because hearing was granted and so there is no point in deciding that motion. But there seems to be pending, however, the question as to the manner of approaching witnesses, particularly as indicated in paras 9 and 11 of the Popovic motion. Reading through the 11th July transcript, it appears that Mr. Nicholls for the OTP had suggested that rather than hastening into a decision on the matter it would be more helpful for all parties to continue discussing what guidelines, if any, ought to be established and followed, and we had agreed with you to give you this opportunity to discuss amongst yourselves a possible list of guidelines which -- consensual list of guidelines. What we would like to know, and of course if you're not in a position to give us an answer now, you can do so tomorrow, is whether there have been ongoing discussions between the parties on the issues still remaining to be discussed and decided, namely in relation to the manner of approaching witnesses, failing which you also need to confirm to us whether we still need to hand down a decision indicating guidelines ourselves. So, please, come back to us on this at the earliest, possibly tomorrow. Not later than tomorrow. Thank you. Apart from what you said in relation to the next witness, there is nothing else. All right. So I think, Madam Usher, you can proceed with bringing the witness in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I still have a bit of a buzz in my ear. I don't know if it's my head or the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had it too. I have this knob which I turned anti-clockwise and it disappeared. I don't know if you have a similar knob.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, that seems to have helped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to welcome you to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You're about to start giving evidence and before you do so, you're required to enter a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth and the whole truth. Please read the text of the solemn declaration aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Todorovic. Please make yourself comfortable. You are now going to be asked a few questions by Mr. McCloskey, who is lead counsel for the Prosecution in this case, and he will then be followed by the Defence teams on cross-examination. Your duty is to answer each question, whoever is putting it to you, truthfully and as briefly as possible but as precisely as possible, too. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Todorovic. Can you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you for the record please state your name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us how old you are?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I work in the catering industry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And everyone here knows that Kladanj is in Bosnia-Herzegovina. All right. And can you tell us, did you do JNA military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember what year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: In 1984, and 1985 actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what kind of position did you have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And when the war broke out in Bosnia, in 1992, can you briefly outline for us the -- your military history?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I fled Kladanj and went to Vlasenica, I signed up with the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was that unit you first signed up with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: First it was the Sekovac brigade, actually the Sekovici brigade, at the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Was that similar to Vlasenica or --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: And later on, it was Vlasenica. Actually, it was the same. I believe that the two shared the same military post number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And after that time period at the Vlasenica/Sekovici unit, as you described, did you move to another unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was in September, early September, 1992. A unit was set up. It was an assault detachment with the Drina Corps. I stayed with them for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: And then I went to the Special Police Brigade, the 2nd Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that would have been under the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was your position in the Special Police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A foot soldier, a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Borovcanin, an accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Borovcanin at that time. I did not see him around. I don't know whether he was in the position that he held later on. But I knew him from my private life, from the municipality where I resided. He resided there as well. I believe that he was either the commander or the chief of police station. He was held in high esteem. He was educated, influential in town. He introduced order to the police and to the town. You have to know that the area had been ridden with a lot of problems before the war and he restored peace and order to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just clarify which town you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So and how long were you in the Special Police, just roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was set up in March, and I stayed with it until mid-June or the beginning of July. I don't know exactly. In any case, I believe it could have been three to four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go after those three to four months?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I left the unit, the Special Police, that is, I joined the Vlasenica Brigade, an intervention unit, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was with that unit until the moment I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The 27th of July 1994, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you rejoin the army after your wounding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when I recovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A unit was set up, the 2nd -- the 10th Sabotage Unit, and I joined that unit. I believe it was either on the 1st of October or the 1st of November, I can't be sure of that. I joined that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us a bit about that unit, where it was located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The sabotage unit was located in Bijeljina and in Vlasenica. It was military post 7572/15 Sarajevo but it was located in Bijeljina and in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what was the purpose of that unit? What was the job of that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That unit was used in depth of the enemy territory to secure certain facilities or persons. It all depended on their importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the soldiers worked behind enemy lines basically in most cases?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us a bit about what you know about the structure? For example, the 10th Sabotage Unit, under what jurisdiction of the army was it under?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was under the authority of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And which of the units were you assigned to in 1995? And you've mentioned Bijeljina and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was the Vlasenica platoon. One part of the troops were deployed in Dragasevac and I belonged to that part of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is Dragasevac a village near Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Maybe four or five kilometres away from Vlasenica, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And was Drazen Erdemovic in the 10th Sabotage Unit in 1995 to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In which area was he assigned, which unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He also belonged to the 10th Sabotage Unit, but he was deployed in Bijeljina. He had been signed up to the Bijeljina part of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. In 1995, can you tell us your rank, if any, and your position, your job?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I was involved in the logistics of the Dragasevac unit, and I also performed all the logistical support task for the Bijeljina squad. I was in charge of the food, the arms, the accommodation, both during the times when the unit was billeted in Dragasevac as well as they were sent into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so you went into the field with the units that you were supplying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you went into the field, did your position change at all, or did you stay as a logistics support person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Throughout all that time, I was in charge of the logistics. I made sure that people had food, that they had accommodation, that they had breakfast in the morning, transportation to wherever they were being taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back a little bit to the -- and you'll find we may repeat ourselves and you may get asked the same questions again. Please bear with us. That's a normal part of -- we try to not do it too often but it's normal. Just go back a bit to this structure. Can you tell us who your commander was in 1995, at the Vlasenica unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: My commander was Mr. Pelemis. His deputy was a lad who had come from I don't know where. His name was Andrija Borovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you have any kind of a rank? I think I asked you that but --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I had the rank that I had received in the army but I had not finished any schools. We just performed certain tasks or competed in various competitions and that's how we gained our ranks. Mine was corporal, and this is what I have in my military booklet, but that wasn't really a rank as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Mr. Pelemis, what was his rank in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe that he was either the second lieutenant or lieutenant in the Republika Srpska army, but he never wore any patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you tell us, as far as you know, who were the authorities above Mr. Pelemis, that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Those were people from the Main Staff, General Ratko Mladic, Mr. Manojlo Milovanovic. Mr. Petar Salapura. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You've mentioned a few other people to us that I'll ask you about as we go along, but let's start with who you've just mentioned, Mr. Petar Salapura. What -- as far as you knew, what was his position in relation to the 10th Sabotage Unit, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but he communicated with the sabotage unit the most. I don't know what his position was. I really wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what branch of the army did you feel he was part of or did you know he was part of, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not a hundred per cent sure whether he was a member of the intelligence structure or the security structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned Tolimir, Mr. Tolimir. What was your knowledge of his position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was he above or below Salapura, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw Mr. Tolimir in Zepa the first time, and I believe that he was a general. That was his rank. And I believe that Petar Salapura was subordinated to Mr. Tolimir, at least judging by their ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware of any contact that Mr. Tolimir had had with the 10th Sabotage Detachment before you saw him in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He never came to our unit. Maybe he assisted -- attended a lineup but we never paid too much attention to all these officers. There were always so many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. You had mentioned the name of an officer named Mr. Beara. Do you know anything about Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a lading suggestive question. I don't think he mentioned that name at all, unless I just missed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Meek is right, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to rephrase your question. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you mention Mr. Beara's name in your interviews with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Again, Judge, I object. That's leading and suggestive. He's indicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We can keep on going around in circles on this. At the end of the day he can always ask the question: Which names did you mention to the Prosecution during the interview? And then you can, of course, try to suggest names and to get a confirmation from him. You go around in circles on a matter like this so at the end of the day it doesn't get you anywhere. I mean, listen, we've all got years and years and years of practice in a courtroom. You know that this is how it works out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think this is really a contentious point. I can ask him to review his statement to see if it refreshes his recollection to anyone else he may have mentioned to us or I can just simply ask him the same question. I really would prefer to skip the intricacies of the adversarial system, unless it's a real issue then I think we should play by that rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we should move on. There are so many ways of dealing with it, Mr. McCloskey. I'm not here to teach anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, this discussion we've had, did this refresh your recollection at all as to anybody else that may have had anything to do with your experience as a soldier at this time period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I only met them in passing by. I saw them talking to my officers. I personally never exchanged a word with any of the officers that I've mentioned. Neither did they ever give me any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Had you mentioned Mr. Beara to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did. I saw Mr. Beara on the Han Pijesak-Vlasenica road. He was exchanging greetings with my commander but that wasn't a significant moment at all. I only saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you just give us a rough time frame when you saw him there on this road? Before or after Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This was before the sabotage detachment, that unit. I can't remember which unit exactly it was. It was either in 1993 or maybe 1992. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And were you aware of him having any contact with the 10th Sabotage Detachment in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to the time period in early July 1995. And can you tell us, did you and your unit have any assignment related to the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We received our assignment on the 10th of July. The task was to prepare the unit to go into the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you get a written order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: If we did, then it was the officer in charge who received it. When he did, he would pass the assignment on to the troops. But the whereabouts of the field where we were supposed to go to was only made known to us ten minutes before we started marching, and it was only then when we were made aware of the assignment -- what the assignment really was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of a written order that was general and was related to this mission?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware of that. I had a piece of paper that had arrived in the unit, and I knew what troops were being sent out, and what things had to be prepared by way of logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you a document. It's P02869. It will come up on your screen, but just for convenience sake I've got an original here that I would like you to be able to look at as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could just hand it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we can see that this is addressed to the command of the 10th Sabotage Detachment and that this order to you was pursuant to a Main Staff order of the intelligence sector. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This is just some of the troops that were sent out on the mission, on the 10th of July 1995. They went to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this a document you saw on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we see at the bottom that it's in the name of Milorad Pelemis but it is signed by Franc Kos. Can you tell us who Franc Kos was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the Bijeljina group, of the Bijeljina Platoon. I did not communicate with him much. I did not know him. The units was of a mixed composition. I'm talking about the Bijeljina Platoon. It consisted of Muslims, Croats. There was a Slovenian, there were people from Serbia, and in Vlasenica, we were a Serb platoon, all the people bore Serbian names, and that's why we did not really trust them. We were not very close. We didn't know how they had joined the unit, and how they had left -- how they left the unit finally when the unit broke up. To this very day, we don't know how this unit came about to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in 2004, where did you get the document from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I had this document on my files that were left behind after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you provided us some other documents as well, and-- didn't you? And we may go over some of those.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about, let's go back to 1995, July 10th, and we see this group of people listed in the document. Did that -- and we see your name on it. As far as you know, did that group of people actually go to the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean the ones that are on this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And what day did they go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can you briefly describe to us when you left your area, where you went and what you did on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We packed our gear in Dragasevac. We waited for the Bijeljina platoon. We boarded the vehicles that we had at our disposal. We came into the vicinity of Zeleni Jadar, where we spent the night, and we didn't move anywhere from Zeleni Jadar. It was a couple of kilometres from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So it would be the morning of the 11th that you would have woken up in Zeleni Jadar. Can you tell us what the unit did that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We had breakfast that day, made some preparations for our future work and we were awaiting instructions and orders from the man in charge for further movement of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was that, the man in charge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was Mr. Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And when -- I don't see his name on this list. When did he join you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He came later, along with Mr. Vukasinovic, the driver. They came in a Golf car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So what orders did you get on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: An order was given on that date to enter the town, the town of Srebrenica, and to capture the town, that we were to be divided into two groups and that we would enter from a plum tree into the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And were you part of one of those groups?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Plum tree group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And all right. And who was the command of your group, of your small group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There was no one heading. We were lined up. We had communication between ourselves. We had Motorola radios and that is how we maintained communication with our central point or centre of communications as a detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Mr. Pelemis remained in command of the entire group?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was leading our movement, and he maintained communication lines all the time with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just briefly describe what you did.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I told you now that we just -- that we -- it was just a walk in the park, that would be ridiculous. We entered the city or the town without any resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: About what time did you actually get into the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly the time, whether it was mid-day, afternoon. Nobody paid attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, just roughly. Just your best idea.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I do believe that it happened in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go in the town, any particular place where you settled in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We went down to the police station. We secured the police station to prevent anyone from tampering with the documents, because that is where the alleged staff of Naser Oric was. We spent all the time there keeping the police station under blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see any superior officers at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: None of these officers did I see prior to the arrival of General Mladic. I believe that he came before General Zivanovic but I don't know exactly whether he was there. I know that General Zivanovic's brother was there but I don't know what he was doing. And a couple of lads from the security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned General Zivanovic for the first time. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Drina Corps. I personally had no contact with him. I never visited him. I never saw him. I wouldn't be able to recognise him even today. So truly ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But did you know who he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't. I just heard comments from other soldiers. There were not even soldiers from our unit. There were some soldiers from elsewhere. They didn't have any insignia and we didn't know to which units they belonged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did General Mladic come by?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what if anything did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He didn't address me personally. He exchanged greetings with a couple of soldiers and the men that were there, soldiers as well. He ordered us to continue the blockade, pending the removal of the material from the SUP, and then he issued an order for them to move towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You say he issued an order for them to move towards Potocari. Who do you mean by "them"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the remaining troops that were there. I don't know whose units these were. Our troops were there. That's for sure. But I don't know to which units they belonged. They didn't have any insignia. They only have tricolour patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The tricolour patches, what was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was a form of the troops having some sort of recognising patches when they embark on a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of the orders of your unit from General Mladic? Or from Pelemis or whoever you may have received an order from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He ordered us to keep the station under blockade until all the important documents were removed and everything inside inspected. After that, we were relieved of duty on the 11th of -- on the evening of the 11th and we were told to retreat and that we had 48 hours to search and to take whatever we wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And I probably confused the issue. Who did you receive that order from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: From the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And where did you stay the night of the 11th? Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We spent the night outside of town, or rather in the suburbs, close to the road leading to Zeleni Jadar. There were three houses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do on the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: A driver, Zeljko Vukovic, and I headed off to Dragasevac in order to prepare the receipt of other unit, that is to prepare the meals for them, before their arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm -- the interpreter may not have gotten the -- may have missed some of the -- where did you say you were heading off to? What town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Via Zeleni Jadar, we went, I don't know the name, it's Kragljivoda, Jezero, Skelani, Favkovici [phoen], Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, Milici, Vlasenica, Dragasevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Dragasevac is your final destination, back to your base, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know roughly what time you got to your base on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Given that it's a long journey, maybe it was 12.00 or 1.00 but I didn't pay attention to the time. The point was for us to get there. We didn't have any time limitations imposed on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you got back to the base, what did you do? Just briefly describe the rest of your day there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: There were female cooks and gate-keepers. I inspected the compound. We parked the lorry. We provided warm water for people to have a bath in the evening. We set up billeting facilities. We prepared dinner for them. We secured the perimeter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did any of the units return that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: They returned on the evening of the 12th, and I'm talking about the remaining troops, but I was there ahead of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Understood. So did you get another assignment sometime after you returned on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Until the remaining soldiers came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then what assignment did you receive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: One of the vehicles went off the road, and Dragan from Trebinje --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the last name of the soldier.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: -- was killed and another soldier I think his name was Mladjen, I think he was a Croat, was also -- was injured as well as Mr. Pelemis, and it all happened on their way back from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Todorovic, could you repeat the name of the person that got killed in this accident because the interpreters didn't hear it well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan Koljivrat, a private from Trebinje, was killed in this accident and that's where he was subsequently buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Todorovic. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what assignment you received then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: This all happened so quickly. First the soldiers took care of the injured. Then we took the private, Koljivrat, to the hospital in Vlasenica, in order to obtain certain papers for the benefit of his family so that they know how he lost his life. And we ourselves saw that he was dead. He didn't need any treatment. We just saw that he was killed instantly. He was just taken to the hospital in order for all the paperwork to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you receive an assignment in relation to his death and his family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: My duty was to take the body from the hospital, to notify his family via the army phone, to establish a line with Trebinje and try to locate members of his family in order to convey this sad news to them that they had lost their son, and thereafter, the usual procedure was followed. We prepared that body. We transported it to Trebinje. We organised the burial. And I did it all myself with the assistance, of course, of other soldiers who were with me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did a group of you go all the way from Vlasenica across over to Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember some of the names that went with you from the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I can remember two drivers, Zeljko Gagic, excuse me, Zeljko Vukovic and Nebojsa Gagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who else do you remember that went along?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Drazen Erdemovic. Srdjan Brijezo. And another three or four soldiers but I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, can you tell us all -- many people may know but can you tell us where Trebinje is in relation to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It's about -- it takes about six or seven hours to drive there. I don't know how can I explain to you where it is. I don't know how many kilometres the exact distance is. I didn't measure it. But I know that it was a long ride. We had to take some roundabout roads that we arrived after midnight where we met the family. They showed us the way to their house. It was a house in the suburb of Trebinje. It was completely made of stone, as I was -- as far as I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is Trebinje very close to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I think it's about 20 kilometres, maybe less, maybe more. Because I saw the road sign and that is, I think, where this sign post was that HVO forces were deployed. That's what I heard. And one could see that from the cemetery where this dead soldier was buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And can you now tell us -- tell us what day was it that you took this very long drive to the Trebinje area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what day was the actual funeral?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And after the funeral, did you go back to the -- to the family home, as is the tradition?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did. And that's what kept us there. His father offered us wine and a bottle of brandy sealed with wax which is the tradition to prepare such a bottle for a son and his wedding, and he was in such a shock he said because we buried him today, I'm going to offer you this brandy. I don't know what kind of tradition that was. So we stayed there longer than planned, and then we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you another document that you gave us. It's P02867. You'll see the B/C/S on the screen. I think it should be fine for this. This is a -- obviously an obituary for Mr. Koljivrat. Do you recognise this obituary? Is this something you gave to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And are the dates correct, as far as you know, regarding his death on the 12th of July and the funeral?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed on the 12th. He was 25 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the funeral was on the 14th, as it states?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think we need that any further. So as -- was it the -- your small unit that you've described with the family that evening, was it everyone with the family, not just yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just roughly what time did you leave the family home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Maybe it was 8.00 or 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did your group go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Back to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you make any stops on the way, any long stops?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we did. We stayed for a while at Pale. This is where Srdjan Brijezo's family was living there. They had fled Sarajevo. And they were living in the settlement made up of weekend cottages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do at Pale?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We took a rest there for a while, had a breakfast because the family offered us something to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: We proceeded towards our base in Dragasevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so just again roughly what time did you get back to the base in Dragasevac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: It was in the morning, 9.00, 10.00 or 11.00 but definitely between 10.00 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this would be what date, then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I switched it off when I should have switched it on. For the record, Mr. Haynes is now present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. You had just told us that your group came back from the funeral about, you said between 10.00 and 11.00 on the morning of the 15th. Can you tell us what happened, what you remember about the 15th at your base after you got back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: When I returned to the base in Dragasevac, we parked the car, the troops who were with me were relieved. I went to the office to search for the commander because I had some gifts that his family had sent him. He wasn't there. I asked a soldier at the gate where Mr. Pelemis was, and he told me that he was either in Bijeljina or at the hospital in Belgrade. I stayed there for a while. I tidied up a little. There were more troops from the unit. They were idle. They were not engaged in any activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What do you remember happening? Any arrivals? Anything you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: After a while, Mr. Pecanac arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not a name we've heard before. Can you tell us who Mr. Pecanac is, a name during your testimony, you didn't mention him before. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was the head of security, general's aide de camp. I don't know how I should put it. He was always with him. He carried out his orders and looked after his security and he had some troops who provided security with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So when you say security for General Mladic, you mean personal security?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Not personal security, but I believe that he was in charge of his personal affairs. He looked after his security together with some other troops that were around him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And it may be a difference between the English -- sometimes English uses the same word for security. But we are talking about security as in safety as opposed to security as in the security branch?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I understand, I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So when you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So what happens with Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: An officer came with him but he did not enter the perimeter of the base. Mr. Popovic. He did not speak to any of the soldiers. He stayed by the car outside the gate and Mr. Pecanac entered and asked Obrenovic for some soldiers. There was a skirmish between the two of them of sorts. I don't know what they argued about. I didn't know at the time. He started shouting. After the argument with Obrenovic he shouted at Vojkovic to gather some people and to send those soldiers with him. I don't know where he took them and I don't know who was supposed to give the authority instead of the commander to let the soldiers go. Mr. Popovic's Golf was parked there all the time. Mr. Popovic did not get involved in any of those things, nor did he communicate with anybody all that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And who, as far as you knew at the time, was this Mr. Popovic person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He was a security officer in the Drina Corps. He used to come to our unit even before the 15th. He would talk to the commander. They hailed from the same area. They probably knew each other from before. He worked in the Drina Corps. He was in charge of the security, as far as I know. He never spoke to any of our soldiers. He never issued any orders to any of us when he came to our unit, he would just greet us but he didn't have any influence on our unit, as far as I know. He never asked any questions or issued any orders to any of our soldiers or any soldier, not even Pelemis. Maybe he conveyed some messages to him in their conversations but he never issued a written order, an order that would come from him; at least I never saw any such order coming from him in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you know what rank he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: How should I know? Those ranks were bestowed upon people over night. I don't know whether anybody completed any education. I don't know if he was a lieutenant-colonel or colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You had mentioned I think before that you thought he was a lieutenant-colonel or a colonel, you weren't sure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was 12 years ago. Even if I knew, I've forgotten. I just know his family name. I believe his name was Vujadin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you mentioned that Pecanac had come in and gotten in an argument with Obrenovic. Is that Zoran Obrenovic, one of the soldiers with the 10th Sabotage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And this --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you actually see Mr. Popovic outside the gate with his car or did someone just tell you that he was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: The gate-keeper told us that Officer Popovic was outside. This person who was working, providing security for the base, I suppose that he must have seen his car and he must have assumed that he was there. I'm sure he knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you, after getting this information, did you actually see Mr. Popovic yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't approach the gate. I was standing some 25 to 30 metres away from the gate. I was standing next to the garage door and the garage was the place where Popovic [as interpreted] and Pecanac had that argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. But did you ever see Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I saw him in town. I saw him when he came to the unit. I saw him during certain events or lineups. He would appear together with the other officers from the Drina Corps, when this was some sort of a festivity or a celebration in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But on the 15th, did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I saw the car but I did not see him personally getting out of the car or talking to anybody. That I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understand you didn't see him talking to anybody but did you see him in the car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I could see a person in the car. I don't know whether there was anybody else with him in the car. I didn't pay too much attention because my attention was drawn by the argument. I tried to calm the two people down but Pecanac ignored me when I asked Zoran what the argument was all about and then he left the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the person you see in the car look like the Popovic you knew?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness already responded to this question more than once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think this is a clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where has he already answered that question according to you, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He already said that he didn't see Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's page 36, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We know exactly what you're referring to but the thing is that going through the part of the transcript, I think definitely calls for a clarification. So perhaps you can rephrase your question, Mr. McCloskey, and put another one by way of trying to clarify what the witness has already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall telling investigators before that Mr. Popovic waited outside his car, outside the base?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He did not get out of the car. He was in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, that's why I asked you to clarify because when Mr. Zivanovic says that the witness never said that he saw Mr. Popovic is basically not correct because the witness has already stated that he did, in lines 36, page 36, lines 10 and 11. "Okay, but did you ever see Mr. Popovic?" The answer was: "Yes, I did." "And where was he had he saw him?" "I saw him in town." So the reason why we asked to clarify because your question was relating to the Popovic that he knew but it is not necessarily related to the time frame that you were asking the witness about when you put that second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it needs to be -- yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can argue with it but I think we all understand the point and I think we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic, let him say what --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is one mistake in the transcript at page 36, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, let me get there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness said the name of Obrenovic, not the name of Popovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what we have in the transcript is Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he said Obrenovic, Obrenovic and Pecanac had arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But unless someone points that out to us we are not in a position to know because we follow the proceedings in English. That's one further reason why you should clarify, Mr. McCloskey. And thank you for pointing that out to us, Mr. Zivanovic. Because otherwise we wouldn't have become aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think Mr. Zivanovic is correct. That is an error. I'm sure the witness said that the argument was between Zoran Obrenovic and Pecanac but I think he can confirm that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to show you some notes that the Federal Bureau of Investigation took when they interviewed you back on the 19th of June in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I object to the procedure the Prosecution is going to attempt to use to clear up a simple point in regards to Mr. Zivanovic's objection and I think he can go back easily to the transcript of what he just said today and clarify it like you had insinuated and I object to using some statement when he can do it very easily by asking him one simple question from his testimony on page 36, line 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't heard the question as yet. I don't know if Mr. McCloskey by referring to this interview or notes resulting from the interview are related to this issue or to some other issue. Perhaps you can clarify that before we can decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's related to the issue of whether or not the witness recalls Mr. Popovic being out of his car or inside his car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He clearly said that he didn't see Mr. Popovic at all either inside the car or outside the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that needs to be clarified, Mr. Zivanovic and if this is one way of clarifying it our decision is that you may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could -- I can show the witness his -- the notes in B/C/S on this -- on this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it right? Was it the FBI?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You recall being interviewed by the FBI, and if we could get some help we'll just show him the B/C/S version of that. And I'm sorry I haven't outlined it for you but if you -- it's in the middle of the document, about the 11th paragraph, it says: "A group of soldiers that included Major Pecanac, General Mladic's aide de camp, was waiting for Todorovic when he got back to Dragasevac, a senior officer named Popovic was also present, although he waited for Pecanac by his Volkswagen Golf outside the driveway's gate." Does that help you remember whether or not this Popovic person was inside the car or outside the car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Switch yours off, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see the document on the display. Ah, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, Mr. President, I just want to clarify that on page 40, line 9 and 10, Mr. McCloskey has indicated that he's going to show this witness some of his -- the witness's notes and that's just not true. This is an FBI report. These aren't notes of the witness. The FBI can write down what they want to write down. It doesn't mean that it is the notes of this witness which Mr. McCloskey insinuated it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I said notes. I didn't insinuate anything. And these are FBI notes as we all know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I recall -- there is nowhere it says that Mr. McCloskey said that he was going to show him his own notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a standard FBI report of a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Now I want to show you some notes that the Federal Bureau of Investigation took." I'm referring to page 39, lines 10 and 11 and 12. "I want to show you some notes that the FBI took when they interviewed you back on the 19th of June 2005." That's what Mr. McCloskey premised --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, pardon me, but I was looking at page 40, line 9 where Mr. McCloskey said, "And if we could, I can show the witness his, the notes in B/C/S."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But I think it's clear enough. Let's make it clear once and for all. These are not notes that were prepared by the witness. They are notes that were prepared by the FBI; isn't that correct, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having clarified that, I suggest you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, does this help your memory at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. If he had appeared, I would have approached him. I don't know what the person from the FBI put in his notes. I stated that the car was his, that a person was seated in the car. If Mr. Popovic had come out, I would have approached him and said hello or he would have approached us. I don't know why he was there on that day, the boss was not there. I didn't really understand what he was doing there with Mr. Pecanac because this gentleman Pecanac he would turn up out of the blue every now and then whenever the mood took him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. When you say the car was his, who do you mean? Whose car was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At the Drina Corps, that he used to drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you also -- do you recall telling the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that Popovic showed up that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: His car, and it was only normal that he was driving it. I wasn't driving it. But I didn't speak to him. I did not have any contact, any conversation, any dialogue with the person in the car. He did not address either me or the gate-keeper or any of the troops, whereas Mr. Pecanac entered the base on his own. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One sentence from his testimony was omitted in the transcript. He said "or someone else" after the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which line on which page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is page 42, line 23, after first sentence, he said "or someone else." His car and it was only normal that he was driving it or someone else. He said it but it was not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was your answer, Mr. Todorovic, to the -- to Mr. McCloskey's question? The question was, "Okay. And do you recall telling the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that Popovic showed up that day?" In the transcript, we have this as the first part of your answer: "His car, and it was only normal that he was driving it." Who would drive that car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The car was driven by the person that the car belonged to. It was wartime. Cars were requisitioned or used by different persons. It could have been a foot soldier on a mission. It could have been the general. This was the car of the Drina Corps that was parked in the garage and it was used by officers, and for officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall what you told the Office of the Prosecutor about Mr. Popovic that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: That it was his car and that it is possible that he was in the car. I did not see the man personally. I never said that I'd seen him. If I'd seen him, I would have said hello. I don't know how my words are being translated because I know that Mr. Popovic did used to come to the unit. I can't say that he didn't. But he never issued any orders to us soldiers. Mr. Popovic never issued us any soldiers [as interpreted]. He worked in the Drina Corps. He performed his duties. I don't know what he did. I'm not aware of that. I can't tell you what he did. I don't know whether he was in charge of security or operations or intelligence. There were various formations, various detachments, but I claim with full responsibility that Mr. Pecanac was the one, he entered the base. I myself did not leave the base in order to see who was driving Mr. Popovic. I don't know whether it was him or not. Maybe he had a driver. Maybe there was another officer. But it was his car. Definitely his car. And he was the one who used this car most often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you've previously just -- you just testified earlier that Mr. Popovic was the security officer for the Drina Corps. Now you've just said you don't know what he was. I know it's not easy to testify but can you clarify that? What was he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. It's not a problem. He was a Drina Corps officer and that's where his office was. I assume that he was a security officer, but I never questioned him about his job. I can only assume that he was the security officer of the Drina Corps. I suppose that he was not an intelligence officer of the Main Staff. I was a foot soldier. I could hardly tell the ranks and those changed very often. I know he was an officer; he had his office in the Drina Corps. I'm sure of that but I don't know whether he was a security officer or not. I can't be 100 per cent sure. I am sure that he was an officer, though, but I never dwelled upon the structure of ranks and things like that. You should ask his superior who bestowed the rank upon him. If I'd had any contact with him, if I'd cooperated with him, if I had collaborated with him then I would be better suited to give you his rank and his official position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep questions and answers as short as possible, particularly the answers. This was long, drawn, unnecessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you believe Mr. Popovic was at your base on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's the objection, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, it's a belief, it's not do you think or do you speculate. Do you believe. Do you have reason to believe that he was there on the 15th of July? We don't want to you speculate, Mr. Todorovic. We just want you to give a truthful answer to the question that has been put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not making any speculations. What I'm saying is that it was possible that he was there because that was his car but I personally didn't see him. There was a -- there was some trees and there was 30 metres between me, where I was, and where he was. He never entered, nor did I go down there. And he didn't address anyone from the car. I'm not speculating. It was his car. There was a man in the car who talked to nobody. And he didn't address anybody. Nobody asked me any details, whether I saw Popovic personally when I was questioned. I said that his car was there. I don't know the licence number. The man was some ten metres to the side of the gate. Nobody approached the car. I didn't. No soldiers did -- didn't. Mr. Pecanac was with Obrenovic. I was some ten metres away from him. And after all this happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's enough for us, Mr. McCloskey. You can proceed with your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd like to show you what you had said to the Office of the Prosecutor on this point because it appears that it may help you remember this incident. And it may be slightly different than you're remembering it now but let me get that for you now so you can look at it. If I can get the statement to the Office of the Prosecutor from 9 December 2004 in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While that's being done, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is not refreshing the witness's recollection. He's trying to impeach the witness. The witness said, never said he didn't have a recollection of it. In fact his told us his recollection of it. It's very clear. There was a person in the car, he couldn't identify that person. He never saw Mr. Popovic. And this is not proper refreshing of any recollection of his own witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Meek, but I think if you read lines 18 -- from line 18, page 45, to line 5 on page 46, you will immediately understand why further clarifications from the witness are necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, just, if you could hand that to him so he can have a chance to look at it, this -- Mr. Todorovic -- begins with paragraph 9 is where we -- where you start talking about this subject. So take a little time to look at that. And -- now, in that statement, it says: "Between 10.00 a.m. and 12 noon, Major Pecanac arrived at Dragasevac, with a security officer, Lieutenant-Colonel, or Colonel Vujadin Popovic. They arrived in two separate vehicles. Pecanac came into the compound whilst Popovic remained on the outside. Pecanac told Zoran Obrenovic to round up some men to deploy somewhere. I've never heard exactly what he said but I saw that Obrenovic had a verbal argument with Pecanac." And then I'm going to just go to the part about Popovic. You go on to say: "All this while, Popovic remained outside the compound area. The group then followed Popovic in a van which I previously used to travel to Trebinje. Popovic drove alone in the VW Golf." Now, today, are you telling us you told the Prosecutor all this and you told what you told the FBI and now you're saying you never saw Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I saw Popovic but it's not written anywhere here that he alighted from the car, that I communicated with him. There was a driver in the car and I suppose that it was Popovic, but I personally didn't see him. It's not written anywhere here that he came out of the car, that I said that that he got out of the car, moved away from it, spoke to anyone. Only Mr. Pecanac spoke to soldier. It says here very clearly his car, actually two cars, Pecanac entered the compound while Popovic remained outside. Since it was his car, I presume he was in the car. And I never said that he got out of the car, moved around, talked to someone, because judging by the car, the make of the car and the licence plate, it was his car. But I didn't see him personally coming out of the car and I never said that. It says clearly here that there were two cars, one was driven by Pecanac and the other belonged to Popovic. I didn't go down to the gate to see whether it was him 100 per cent. I only presumed that since it was his car, he was the one driving it. I didn't say anything to compromise these people. I didn't say anything incorrectly. It is my statement and it was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you told us that you heard from the gate-keeper that Mr. Popovic was outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to another subject. The argument you saw between Mr. Pecanac and Mr. -- And I don't think we need that any more.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't need it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if you do need it, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us what you heard Pecanac tell Zoran Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: He asked him to give him a group of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me. I think the question has been asked and answered. I could go back. I recall specifically this witness stating that he did not hear the conversation, the argument between these two individuals, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We got briefly into it. We haven't had a chance to flush it out at all, and that's what I'm doing. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It hasn't been elaborated more than having a passing comments on it. So please go -- proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you told us that you saw this argument. Can you tell us what you heard of the argument, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: At the moment this conversation was going on, but after Zoran and I left the compound, I asked him what this officer wanted, and he said that he wanted a group of men for a certain job. I didn't give the permission for men because I didn't have an authorisation from the commander Pelemis, because he was the one who can give direct order or sign an order for anyone to leave the base. If anyone got killed without such an order, it entails certain responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understand. What did -- what did Zoran Obrenovic tell you about this job, in details?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody talked to us soldiers about any mission, whether -- where the unit was going. Upon return from the field there was no conversation about that because we had contracts signed as professional soldiers with the staff. Therefore we didn't discuss where any group had gone. Upon return we would just return the weapons and other equipment into the depot. Whatever was to be used again was stored in the depot. What was not usable any longer was written off, and that was how it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the Office of the Prosecutor that Zoran had mentioned a particular place and meeting a particular person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: After Pecanac was giving order to Vojkovic, soldier Vojkovic, when he shouted at him following the argument he told him to round up the men, that he had a meeting in Zvornik with a colonel or whatever he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you tell us a name when you spoke to us about what that colonel's name was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I believe that his name was Beara. That he had to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that what you told us, that he had to -- round up this group, go to Zvornik and see Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN TODOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that he had gone to Zvornik. I didn't say that men went to Zvornik. They just left the base and went towards Sekovici and there were five combat lines, one to Kladanj, Sekovici, Klisa, Boskovici, but nobody asked me anything where the troops might have gone. I said I didn't know. Maybe they were providing security for Pecanac and Beara. Maybe they were providing escort for some other officer. I didn't have any written order as to where to deploy the troops. Once Mr. Pecanac rounded them up, he took them from the compound down the road which is a fork road.
